title: Bollinger Band breakout first-order + rebalance scalping grid
entry_long: first order: candle ID2 closes below Lower Band and is bearish (min body 100 pips), candle ID1 bullish, price crosses above resistance line drawn at ID2 close (breakout) -> buy; also manual trigger via on-chart button
entry_short: first order: candle ID2 closes above Upper Band and is bullish (min body 100 pips), candle ID1 bearish, price crosses below support line drawn at ID2 close (breakout) -> sell; also manual trigger via button
exit: close all when unrealized profit > 50 USD (rebalance basket close); no SL/TP on individual orders
escalation_cap: max 1000 open orders (broker cap ~1000-position limit); manual trigger lot via Edit Field can exceed 0.01
buildon_idea: add explicit position-cap well below broker max (e.g. 200) and add spread/time filter to skip sideways sessions; consider closing partial baskets instead of all-at-once to reduce spread bleed
novelty_note: rebalance grid (buy when price rises, sell when price falls) is a known scalping style; first-order breakout-off-Bollinger-Band trigger adds some selectivity but core risk is order-count explosion in sideways markets

title: RSI-triggered first order + rebalance scalping grid
entry_long: first order only: RSI < 30 (oversold) -> buy 0.01, no SL/TP, once-per-bar; after first order, rebalance logic buys when current close > previous close and previous candle bullish
entry_short: first order only: RSI > 70 (overbought) -> sell 0.01, no SL/TP, once-per-bar; after first order, rebalance logic sells when current close < previous close and previous candle bearish
exit: close all buy+sell when unrealized profit > 50 USD, then reset lot counters; manual close-all button also available
buildon_idea: already capped at max_order; add a large-timeframe trend filter (as narrator suggests) to only assist rebalance in trend direction, reducing sideways spread bleed; consider linear/log lot-scaling for the manual assist button instead of arbitrary sizes
novelty_note: same rebalance-grid mechanism as EX175 first video but with RSI-based first-order trigger instead of Bollinger breakout; weakness explicitly acknowledged by narrator is sideways markets causing slow spread-driven drawdown

title: Admin: send chart screenshot to Telegram bot on order open
entry_long: price crosses above EMA period 5, once-per-bar -> buy 0.1 lot, SL/TP 60 pips, then capture chart screenshot and send to Telegram
entry_short: price crosses below EMA period 5, once-per-bar -> sell 0.1 lot, SL/TP 60 pips, then capture chart screenshot and send to Telegram
buildon_idea: admin/tooling video (Telegram bot setup + screenshot notification integration); the EMA5 cross entry itself is a trivial placeholder, not the point of the lesson
novelty_note: tutorial is about MT4-to-Telegram screenshot notification wiring (BotFather token, chat ID, allow web request URL), not a trading strategy

title: GRD paired buy/sell hedge with directional lot escalation on losing side
entry_long: first order: no condition, opens both buy 0.01 and sell 0.01 simultaneously if no position exists; subsequent buy adds: if current price < previous buy open price (losing) and 300-pip spacing clear, add buy with lot = prior lot + 0.01 (linear-add); if price > previous buy open (winning) and spacing clear, add buy at fixed 0.01
entry_short: mirror of buy: first order paired with buy; subsequent sell adds: if price > previous sell open (losing) and 300-pip spacing, add sell with lot = prior lot + 0.01; if price < previous sell open (winning) and spacing clear, add sell at fixed 0.01
exit: close all buy+sell when combined unrealized profit > 5 USD, reset lot variables; cut-loss: close all if combined loss > -2000 USD, reset
escalation_cap: n/a (no explicit volume cap stated in this video; protected only by -2000 USD cut-loss)
buildon_idea: add volume_upper_limit cap on the linear-add side (only cut-loss money currently bounds risk); pair-hedge concept (buy+sell simultaneous, escalate only the losing side) is a genuinely distinct build-on idea worth isolating from the martingale label
novelty_note: member-submitted idea: open both directions at once so the winning side's profit offsets the losing side's escalating lot; narrator reports tested profitable through full year 2025 with cut-loss triggering multiple times but account surviving

title: GRD paired buy/sell hedge, trend-mode single-side operation
symbol: unspecified (tested on GOX/gold-style volatile symbol implied)
entry_long: first order: opens both buy and sell 0.01 regardless of condition (once); mode_buy=true enables buy-side correction: if price < prior buy open (losing), add buy every 300 pips with lot += 0.01 (lot_plus); if price > prior buy open (winning), add buy every 300 pips at fixed lot_start_buy 0.01
entry_short: mode_sell=true enables sell-side correction mirrored: if price > prior sell open (losing), add sell every 300 pips with lot += 0.01; if price < prior sell open (winning), add fixed lot_start_sell 0.01; user manually sets mode_buy=true/mode_sell=false when higher-TF trend is up (and vice versa) before running
exit: close all when unrealized profit > 5 USD reset; cut-loss close-all at -2000 USD reset
escalation_cap: n/a (only cut-loss -2000 USD bounds it; volume_upper_limit not emphasized in this video)
buildon_idea: key doctrine stressed by narrator: must pick mode_buy/mode_sell matching the higher-timeframe trend before running, else correction becomes hard and drawdown deep; add explicit volume cap and an automated trend filter (e.g. EMA slope) instead of manual mode selection; backtest shown: 3 months, 1570 orders, +20% return
novelty_note: same GRD hedge-pair concept as first EX177 video but explains the critical trend-selection usage rule and demonstrates a 3-month backtest (+20%, ~1570 orders) using high-spread standard account

title: EMA 9/26/200 alignment entry with trailing-stop and capped martingale (gold, high-volatility regime)
entry_long: no open position; candle ID1 bullish (open<close); EMA9 above EMA200; EMA9 above EMA26; (price crosses above EMA9 OR price crosses above EMA26); current close > current open -> buy 0.01, martingale x2 on loss, capped volume_upper_limit 5 lots, no SL/TP (managed via trailing stop)
entry_short: mirror: candle ID1 bearish; EMA9 below EMA200; EMA9 below EMA26; (price crosses below EMA9 OR EMA26); current close < current open -> sell 0.01, martingale x2 on loss, capped at 5 lots, no SL/TP
exit: trailing stop 500 pips / step 5 pips (backtest setting; recommend step 1 in live use), immediate start
buildon_idea: already capped at 5 lots; narrator explicitly justifies martingale here because underlying win-rate > loss-rate per original long-run test; flat-lot test recommended to confirm entry edge independent of martingale before trusting the 200%+ backtest result; test period 2024-01 to 2025-05 shown +200%+ on $10k, Max relative DD ~49.88%
novelty_note: simple 3-EMA alignment + pullback confirmation (no candlestick pattern, just directional close checks) combined with wide-trail management; positioned by narrator specifically as a safer alternative to accumulation-style EAs during extreme gold volatility (10,000+ point daily swings)

title: Gold Robot EA: EMA 9/26/200 alignment + bullish/bearish engulfing entry, martingale x2 capped 2 lots, trailing stop, time filter
entry_long: EMA9 above EMA200 at ID1; EMA9 crossing above EMA26 at ID1; bullish engulfing pattern (ID2 bearish with min body, ID1 bullish, body ID1 > body ID2) -> buy 0.01, martingale x2 on loss, capped 2 lots, no SL/TP, time filter 14:00-22:00 server time
entry_short: mirror: EMA9 below EMA200, EMA9 crossing below EMA26, bearish engulfing (ID2 bullish, ID1 bearish, body ID1 > body ID2) -> sell 0.01, martingale x2, capped 2 lots, no SL/TP, same time filter
exit: trailing stop 500 pips / step 100 pips (backtest fast setting; use step 1 in production per narrator)
buildon_idea: already capped at 2 lots; flat-lot test first to isolate entry edge from martingale contribution; try linear/log lot law as safer variant; test shown 2024-01 to 2025-04, ~4000 orders, +200%+ profit
novelty_note: simple EMA-align + engulfing; common pattern combo — low novelty on its own, but the tight time filter (14:00-22:00) and 2-lot martingale cap are concrete, reusable risk parameters; this is the schema's hand-built ground-truth anchor card

title: Multigroup Scalping EA with Double Hammer entry, RSI toggle, and reverse-trend group correction (original)
entry_long: no buy position in group1; price above EMA100; candle ID1 is doji (lower wick > upper wick, upper wick > body); candle ID2 has lower wick > upper wick (hammer shape); optional RSI<30 filter if scalping_mode=false -> buy 0.01 (volume_upper_limit 0.1), group1
entry_short: mirror: price below EMA100; ID1 doji (upper wick > lower wick, lower wick > body); ID2 upper wick > lower wick (inverted hammer); optional RSI>70 filter if scalping_mode=false -> sell 0.01 (volume_upper_limit 0.1), group2
exit: per-group: after 2+ orders, trailing stop (ATR-adjusted) manages profit-taking on the winning (follow-trend) side; losing (reverse-trend) side adds correction orders every 60 pips, lot += 0.01 stepped after every 5 correction trades, closes group at unrealized profit > 5 USD; safe mode cuts loss if correction orders exceed 30 or a large impulse candle (time-bomb) appears
escalation_cap: safe-mode cut-off at 30 correction orders per side (optional, default off); no explicit lot cap stated beyond step increments
buildon_idea: turn on safe_mode by default (cut-loss at 30 orders + impulse-candle detection) rather than leaving it off; add hard volume_upper_limit on correction-side lot growth; double-hammer + EMA100 trend filter + RSI toggle is a distinctive, testable entry worth isolating from the martingale correction engine
novelty_note: builds on an earlier EX8 double-hammer concept, adding multigroup (independent buy/sell magic groups) architecture and a scalping-mode vs RSI-filtered safety toggle; narrator stresses trading with the higher-TF trend for easier recovery

title: Multigroup Scalping Double Hammer revise 1: stepped lot AND stepped distance escalation for deeper drawdown tolerance
entry_long: same double-hammer + EMA100 + optional RSI<30 filter as original (EX179 7Op2LWd3LCU) -> buy 0.01 group1, volume_upper_limit 0.1
entry_short: same mirrored double-hammer + EMA100 + optional RSI>70 filter -> sell 0.01 group2, volume_upper_limit 0.1
exit: ATR-scaled trailing stop once group has 2+ orders (winning side); losing side: correction orders every git_distance pips (starts 60), and every 5 correction trades BOTH lot (+0.01) AND git_distance (x2, e.g. 60->120->240) step up together; group closes at unrealized profit > a scaled close_money formula (close_money + orderCount/stepCount * close_money) to avoid negative-close-on-large-basket; stuck-order cleanup: wait 30s after close, re-arm correction mode if positions remain
escalation_cap: no explicit max-order cap in this revision (added in next revise, JLV0REF-oUQ); risk bounded only by widening distance per step
buildon_idea: add an explicit max correction-order cap (fixed in the next revision at 50); the dual lot+distance stepping (both x2 every 5 trades) is a concrete, reusable drawdown-tolerance technique worth extracting into a generic 'martingale distance-stepping' module
novelty_note: incremental improvement over the original (7Op2LWd3LCU): adds simultaneous distance-stepping alongside lot-stepping specifically to let the same account survive roughly 2x the prior point-drawdown; also introduces the scaled close_money formula to prevent negative-balance basket closes

title: Multigroup Scalping Double Hammer revise 2 (forward-test candidate): capped correction orders, ATR trailing, RSI/scalping toggle
entry_long: no buy in group1; price above EMA200; ID2 lower wick > upper wick; ID1 doji (lower wick > upper wick, upper wick > body); optional RSI(7)<30 filter if scalping_mode=false -> buy 0.01, volume_upper_limit 0.1, group1
entry_short: mirror: price below EMA200; ID2 upper wick > lower wick; ID1 doji (upper wick > lower wick, lower wick > body); optional RSI(7)>70 filter -> sell 0.01, volume_upper_limit 0.1, group2
exit: once group has 2+ orders, ATR-adjusted trailing stop (base 60 pips x ATR-derived multiplier, step 1 pip) manages the follow-trend side; losing side adds correction orders at git_distance_RTB/RTS (doubling every 5 trades), lot stepping +0.01 every 5 trades, capped at max_order 50 corrections per side; closes at unrealized profit > scaled close_money formula; 30-second stuck-order cleanup routine on both sides
buildon_idea: already capped at 50 orders/side; this is presented by the author as 1 of 20 EAs entering live forward-testing — good NEVER-TOUCHED/build-on candidate; recommend flat-lot test to isolate entry edge, then verify the ATR-trailing + distance-doubling correction engine on out-of-sample data before relying on capped-martingale safety alone
novelty_note: final revision of the double-hammer multigroup EA series; adds hard order cap (50) missing from revise 1, keeps ATR-adaptive trailing and dual lot/distance stepping; explicitly slated by the creator for real forward-testing among 20 candidate EAs
